what_matters.head: Nvidia fell another 5.5% on Tuesday, about 2.3 times its usual daily move, on twice its average volume. It is down 18.3% over five sessions.
what_matters.detail: On Tuesday The Information reported that Alice Huang's relationship with Jensen Huang could have helped at least $7.5B of Nvidia chips reach Chinese companies, citing two people who know her and corporate records (via Yahoo Finance; The Information's article was not read). The stock briefly fell below $4 trillion in market value that afternoon (CNBC). Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co put the chance that Huang is removed at about 15% and said the board's investigation could take four to six weeks (CNBC). Nvidia reports results on 17 Nov.

what_matters.head: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Excluding food and energy they rose 0.3%, against a 0.2% forecast.
what_matters.detail: There is no year-on-year figure this time: the government shutdown stopped the statistics bureau from collecting October 2025 prices (CNBC). After the report traders fully priced a quarter-point Fed rate rise at the 8–9 Dec meeting, and put the odds of a half-point rise at 13.6%, up from about zero (CME FedWatch via CNBC). Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said she sees a need for two more quarter-point rises (CNBC). The 10-year yield's 12-basis-point rise is in the Markets row.

what_matters.head: CoreWeave's Q3 revenue beat what analysts expected and it raised its full-year forecast. The shares rose 7.9% after hours.
what_matters.detail: Details under Earnings. The after-hours move is not in Tuesday's US closing prices.

out.text: Q3 revenue was $3.66B, up 168% from a year earlier. Analysts expected $3.55B (LSEG) and the company's own forecast was $3.4–3.6B. Adjusted loss was 95 cents a share against an expected $1.16 (LSEG); net loss was $709M, against $110M a year earlier. The company raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $13.0–13.3B from $12.4–13.2B, and its adjusted operating income forecast to $1.275–1.375B from $960M–1.15B. It expects $37–39B of capital spending this year. Backlog was $132.5B, up from $104B in June. All from CNBC. The shares fell 0.5% in Tuesday's session and rose 7.9% after hours.

recent.headline: Nvidia fell another 5.5% on Tuesday, about 2.3 times its usual daily move, on twice its average volume. It is down 18.3% over five sessions.
US stocks had their biggest rally in about seven months on Monday: the S&P 500 fund rose 2.4% and the chip fund 7.5%.
Chip stocks bounced on Friday after their worst sell-off since 2020: the chip fund rose 3.5% and AMD 11%.
Wall Street's AI stocks sold off hard: the S&P 500 fund fell 4.4%, about 6.6 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund 12.2%.
Wall Street rose after the Democratic sweep, led by Microsoft and Amazon, while chip and data-centre stocks fell.
